entry.title: OpenSandbox 1.3.0-rc.2
entry.content:
Second release candidate on the 1.3.0 feature line, cut from release-1.3.0-rc.1 (2026-11-16). Baseline for every section is release-1.3.0-rc.1; rc users on that tag should upgrade. rc releases publish images but hold packages — SDK/CLI artifacts ship at the 1.3.0 stable bump.

Highlights

  • Rootfs-only snapshots now cover native (S3) sandboxes: create_snapshot(mode="rootfsOnly") works end to end for sandboxes on either artifact path — native S3 templates and OCI/OverlayBD templates alike; capture qualification derives from the deployment itself, and an unqualified node fails the snapshot instead of silently producing a full artifact (#2900 #2893 fast-sandbox#181 fast-sandbox#223 fast-sandbox#225)
  • BatchSandbox clean exits finally terminate: a sticky Completed terminal phase replaces the Succeed → Pending limbo that kept an exit-0 sandbox reported as running until expiry deletion (#2715)
  • Two silent workspace-loss races fixed: on Docker, a successful renewal can no longer commit while a concurrently firing expiration deletes the live sandbox and its metadata (#2892); on Kubernetes, expiry deletion carries UID/resourceVersion preconditions so a stale informer copy cannot delete a just-renewed sandbox (#2905)

Server

  • Native (S3) sandboxes accept mode="rootfsOnly" on the public lifecycle API: the server drops its OCI-only preflight mirror, leaving mode compatibility to the FastPath gate (no intent is persisted on rejection) and the Fastlet's fail-closed node re-check; Docker and Kubernetes runtimes still return 409 (#2900)
  • Pool and allocation logic moves behind a WorkloadProvider SPI: deployments with non-BatchSandbox workload providers no longer fail on hardcoded pools.sandbox.opensandbox.io lookups, and /v1/pools on a provider without OSB-managed Pool CRDs returns a clean 501 KUBERNETES::POOL_NOT_SUPPORTED (#2884)
  • Docker renewal is serialized with the per-sandbox lifecycle lock: previously a concurrently firing expiration could delete a running sandbox and its metadata after renew-expiration had already returned 200 (#2892)
  • BatchSandbox Completed maps to the public Terminated state with reason SANDBOX_COMPLETED, carrying the controller's exit detail and completion time; pause/resume on a completed sandbox is rejected explicitly (#2715)
  • A snapshot informer watching a CRD that is not installed (LIST 404) logs a single warning that names the informer instead of a full traceback every 30 seconds (#2875)
  • Smaller fixes: a malformed tenant-provider ttl (null, negative, NaN/Infinity) falls back to the 30-second default instead of failing the lookup or caching forever (#2704); one PoolService/K8sClient is shared across /pools requests instead of rewriting the process-global kube config per request (#2852); list pagination for sandboxes, templates, and snapshots is consolidated with byte-identical responses (#2860); metadata patch validation is shared between the Kubernetes, Docker, and fast-sandbox backends (#2863)

SDKs

  • Code-interpreter readiness is bounded by the ready timeout in Python, JavaScript, and C#: a stalled health probe no longer keeps CodeInterpreter.create() waiting past ready_timeout / readyTimeoutSeconds / ReadyTimeoutSeconds (#2856 #2857 #2858)
  • exit_code / exitCode is populated after codes.run() in Python and JavaScript, matching Kotlin, C#, and Go: 0 on completion, otherwise the error's numeric exit value (#2854)

Python

  • Streamed file downloads keep execd's structured error: a 404 carries error.code and the request id, and a 429 raises SandboxRateLimitException with retry_after instead of a generic exception without the response body (#2696)

JavaScript

  • File download and upload failures surface the server's error code and message instead of a hand-built UNEXPECTED_RESPONSE, matching every other filesystem call (#2700)

C#

  • SSE streams (commands, code, isolated sessions, and the code interpreter) are bounded by a per-read timeout of max(RequestTimeoutSeconds, 30s): a stream that goes silent — for example after the sandbox was paused — now fails instead of blocking forever (#2848)

Controller

  • BatchSandbox gains a sticky Completed terminal phase for a clean exit-0 main container: previously status.phase regressed from Succeed back to Pending until expireTime deleted the CRD, so every consumer kept reporting the sandbox as running for the whole TTL; a completed sandbox skips pod replacement and task scheduling, and pause/resume intents are refused with a SandboxCompleted condition (#2715)
  • Status writes carry a resourceVersion precondition, so a stale runtime view can no longer overwrite a freshly written PauseFailed/ResumeFailed condition — losing that condition also silently broke the server's pause/resume retry path (#2877)
  • All per-object in-memory controller state is forgotten when a BatchSandbox is deleted or replaced under the same name, so a successor no longer inherits stale scale expectations, pod-recovery budgets, or task schedulers (#2861)
  • Smaller fixes: deletion can stop a task by name even when the stored shard patch is malformed, instead of sticking in Terminating forever (#2554); scale expectations that stay unsatisfied past the timeout are dropped so pod creation resumes, like the Pool controller (#2851); snapshot template tests no longer write the process-global time.Local under -race (#2885)

Execd

  • Disk telemetry arrives over OTLP: per-mount usage gauges (execd.system.disk.usage_bytes / total_bytes) with mountpoint/fstype/source attributes, plus cumulative sandbox IO counters (execd.system.disk.io.bytes / io.operations) — each mount stat is bounded by a 2-second timeout so a stale network mount cannot stall the pipeline, and IO prefers sandbox cgroup accounting with a /proc/diskstats fallback (#2912)
  • Foreground command timeouts are reported as CommandTimeout instead of CommandExecError, with the requested timeout recorded in the traceback, logs, and command status (#2684)
  • POST /code no longer hangs forever when the kernel's completion signal is lost: finalization is bounded by a reply-anchored deadline (new --jupyter-reply-finalize-timeout flag, default 2s, restarted on output silence) so the stream closes with a terminal event and the session lock is released (#2804)
  • A /command output line longer than 16 MiB is delivered in UTF-8-boundary pieces instead of being buffered without limit — a 200 MB line previously OOM-killed execd (#2729)
  • Rename batches are validated before any item moves: a missing or empty path returns 400 up front instead of moving the daemon's working directory or partially applying the batch (#2818); an empty expanded path is rejected in every file API, closing the {"": {"mode": 700}} chmod-on-working-directory hole (#2897)
  • /metrics/watch actually sends an update every second as documented, instead of one every two seconds (#2853)
  • Smaller fixes: execution tracking is shared between the three streaming handlers with unchanged metrics (#2862); isolated-session non-zero exits use a typed error so ExitError classification survives future message changes (#2864); rename tests that assumed ${} expands to empty are dropped (#2899)

Networking

egress

  • Credential-vault resolvers now receive the outbound request headers (minus a structural/hop-by-hop denylist, capped at 64 headers and 8 KiB per value, failing closed with 407), completing OSEP-0025's header-bound signature support so exchange resolvers can re-sign schemes like SigV4 and ACS (#2917)
  • [EXPERIMENTAL] The credential-bound Fast Sandbox campaign advances on the readiness and verification fronts: an Actions v1 data-plane-ready Hook waits up to 50 ms for the subject snapshot acknowledgement, turning the guaranteed first-create rejection in this mode into millisecond readiness (#2922); denied TLS handshakes close the client transport instead of leaving it to time out (#2886); and the integration environment gains opt-in mode wiring with honest BLOCKED/NOT_RUN reporting (#2850), trusted TLS protocol fixtures (#2876), a subject-isolation and recovery verifier with a serial credential-bound CI leg and first real KVM acceptance evidence (#2881), restart-recovery tests (#2888 #2906), and operator/client documentation for bindings and persistent connections (#2910). The feature remains opt-in; all and unset behavior is unchanged.
  • Upstream TLS verification failures are reported in Egress logs with a connection ID and a fixed reason code (for example self_signed), so a 502 no longer requires verbose proxy output to diagnose; no hostnames, certificates, or credentials are emitted (#2918)
  • Policy targets written with a trailing root dot (pypi.org., *.github.com.) now match like their dot-less spelling — previously they were silently inert and fell through to defaultAction (#2810)
  • Smaller fixes: the fast-sandbox nftables applier reuses the sidecar's helpers, so a failed batch is retried only when the target table was actually missing (#2865)

Fast Sandbox

  • Rootfs-only snapshots extend to native (S3) sandboxes upstream: FastPath admits RootfsOnly at the gRPC gate for native artifacts (fast-sandbox#223), capture qualification self-derives from the standard managed VMM directory and StateRoot, dropping the FAST_SANDBOX_ROOTFS_QUALIFICATION profile (fast-sandbox#225), and native delivery ships with template-state import and restore-manifest readiness fixes (fast-sandbox#181 fast-sandbox#212 fast-sandbox#214) — carriers (#2893 #2900)
  • FSEP-0003 Fastlet control authentication ships: fastlets authenticate the control API with ServiceAccount tokens verified via JWKS, the controller derives its default caller allow list from its own namespace, and the base chart grants the fenced token-minting Role plus anonymous issuer discovery (fast-sandbox#207 #2900 #2871)
  • Guest wall clocks are calibrated after restore and crash-recovery resume: Firecracker microVMs have no RTC, so a restored guest previously believed the snapshot moment was still now — breaking TLS certificate validation, token expiry, and cron schedules inside the guest (#2900 fast-sandbox#218)
  • An optional FastPath gRPC-Web listener (HTTP/1.1 protobuf, same RPC methods) can be enabled with the new controller.fastpathHTTPPort chart value (default 0, off); ingress gateway and server keep native gRPC and are unaffected (#2938 fast-sandbox#234)
  • The all-in-one (--role=all) controller is enforced to a single replica: chart values with more than one replica are rejected and upgrades use the Recreate strategy so two controllers never reconcile the same SandboxPool concurrently (#2901)
  • Security: Go dependency and toolchain vulnerabilities in the companion image builds are remediated upstream (#2938 fast-sandbox#203)
  • FSEP-0004 (chunked snapshot transfer) and FSEP-0005 (rootfs-only create CPU/memory overrides) land as design proposals with no behavior change (#2938 fast-sandbox#216 fast-sandbox#219)

Misc

  • OSEPs: OSEP-0028 proposes CPU and memory overrides for RootfsOnly sandbox creation via the existing resourceLimits field, reusing POST /sandboxes; it is already in implementation (#2902 #2908)
  • E2B shim (OSEP-0027) [EXPERIMENTAL]: the new components/e2b-shim Go module lands with adapter/router skeletons and liveness endpoints plus component CI (#2920), then validated non-secret configuration loading (#2932); ownership is assigned via CODEOWNERS (#2931). No E2B routes yet.
  • Charts: the Kubernetes minimum is raised to 1.22 across all sub-charts and release metadata — Helm rejects installs on 1.21 clusters (#2874)
  • Docs: the lifecycle API and spec state explicitly that a DELETE 204 means deletion accepted, not confirmed runtime termination, and that a later 404 must not be read as termination (#2738)
  • CI: the host GOPROXY is passed into Go-based integration image builds, unblocking dependency-remediation PRs on restricted hosts (#2925); fast-sandbox PR gates run a single egress leg with per-PR cancellation instead of always occupying the KVM runner with both legs (#2911)

Upgrade & Compatibility

  • Kubernetes 1.21 no longer supported: all charts gate on >=1.22.0-0; upgrade the cluster before installing (#2874)
  • BatchSandbox Completed rollout order: the CRD must be applied before the new controller — an old CRD rejects the new phase with a validation error. Helm installs both together; operators upgrading separately apply the CRD first. Clients mapping CRD phases see the new Completed value, and the public lifecycle state becomes Terminated with reason SANDBOX_COMPLETED (#2715)
  • Native templates must be rebuilt for rootfs-only capture: native template builds now always inject guest control and validate freeze/thaw at build time, and capture from older native templates fails closed (#2900)
  • execd foreground timeouts: CommandTimeout replaces CommandExecError; callers matching error names must handle the new name, and timeout status text now includes the requested duration (#2684)
  • execd rename validation: empty-string src/dest are rejected with 400; callers relying on empty strings to select the current or session-view directory send an explicit path such as "." (#2818)
  • Egress trailing-dot rules take effect: rules written with a trailing root dot were silently inert before and now enforce like their dot-less spelling; review policies — especially deny rules under a default-allow policy — when adopting (#2810)
  • Fast Sandbox upgrades: upgrade the chart and companion images together — control-auth fastlets fail closed without the base chart's token-minting RBAC (#2871 #2900); the all-in-one controller rejects replicaCount > 1 and upgrades carry a brief FastPath interruption under the Recreate strategy (#2901); the gRPC-Web listener stays off unless controller.fastpathHTTPPort is set (#2938)
  • Images: opensandbox/<component>:release-1.3.0-rc.2 (all three registries; fsb images for fast-sandbox)
  • Packages: unchanged — SDK/CLI artifacts publish at the 1.3.0 stable release
  • Charts: render from this tag (helm template ./manifests/charts/opensandbox)
  • Kubernetes: supported range v1.22 – v1.34
  • Skew: server ↔ CLI/SDK same line supported; ±1 minor warns

entry.title: OpenSandbox 1.3.0-rc.1
entry.content:
First release candidate on the 1.3.0 feature line, cut from release-1.2.1 (2026-11-13). Headline: fast-sandbox rootfs-only snapshots reach the public lifecycle API across all five SDKs, and the OSEP-0018 execd-as-init topology becomes the server default. Also notable: request admission and fenced teardown for credential-bound egress subjects, configurable Fastlet Proxy resources, and the removal of the deprecated DevOps plain-text diagnostics surface. Baseline for every section is release-1.2.1. rc releases publish images but hold packages — SDK/CLI artifacts ship at the 1.3.0 stable bump.

Highlights

  • Rootfs-only snapshots on the public API: create_snapshot(mode="rootfsOnly") in all five SDKs — kilobyte-scale, CPU-portable artifacts that restore by cold boot; full remains the default and pause/resume checkpoints stay full-only (#2709 #2835)
  • execd-as-init becomes the default: the server injects EXECD_INIT=1 so execd owns the sandbox process tree (child reaping, signal forwarding, container lifecycle), and a new privilege-reduction guide documents pairing it with the hardening floor (#2825 #2830)
  • Fast Sandbox hardening: Fastlet Proxy CPU/memory resources become configurable through the chart, RootfsOnly snapshot qualification self-derives from the deployed Firecracker bundle, and experimental credential-bound egress advances with request admission, drain fencing, transport teardown, and transition metrics (#2870 #2709 #2794 #2836 #2841 #2838)

Server

  • Fast-sandbox rootfs-only snapshot mode is wired through the public lifecycle API: CreateSnapshotRequest.mode: full | rootfsOnly (default full) with a read-only top-level Snapshot.mode, persisted across SQLite, PostgreSQL, and the one-shot migration; Docker and Kubernetes runtimes reject rootfsOnly in preflight with 409, and the fsb runtime mirrors the FastPath OCI gate before any intent is persisted (#2709)
  • runtime.execd_run_as_init now defaults to true: the server injects EXECD_INIT=1 so bootstrap execs into execd --init; set it to false to keep the classic background-and-wait topology (#2825)
  • The deprecated DevOps plain-text diagnostics surface is removed; the stable Diagnostics API (context, scoped logs/events) is unchanged, and diagnostics/logs/events now require scope (#2826)
  • Security fixes: volumeMounts.subPath values carrying Windows-separator traversal (foo\..\secret) or a leading backslash are rejected, closing a volume-root escape on Windows nodes (#2749); secure-access signing keys are no longer echoed in config-validation errors, including the OPENSANDBOX_SECURE_ACCESS_KEYS env path (#2778)
  • Pool capacity specs where bufferMin exceeds bufferMax are rejected with 422, preventing the controller's create/delete oscillation; pools already applied via kubectl still list (#2801)
  • The server dials host-mapped sandbox ports at docker.publish_host, so the server-side proxy and the egress sidecar readiness probe work when ports are published on a specific address (#2846)
  • Smaller fixes: docker.pids_limit = 0 disables the PID limit as documented (#2786); a malformed template-list metadata filter returns 400 INVALID_METADATA_FORMAT instead of a silently empty page (#2790); renew-intent queue payloads that are valid JSON but not objects are skipped like any other malformed intent instead of logging a full worker-error traceback for each (#2791); reserved-metadata PATCH rejections return the canonical SANDBOX::INVALID_METADATA_LABEL code on the shared Kubernetes/fsb helper and the Docker service (#2793 #2796)

SDKs

  • Snapshot mode (full | rootfsOnly) is exposed across JavaScript, Kotlin, C#, and Go, completing the Python SDK from #2709: an omitted mode stays off the wire for legacy servers, and responses without the field read back as full (#2835)
  • Code-interpreter runtime probes require a confirmed zero exit in Python, JavaScript, and Kotlin, matching Go and C#: CodeInterpreter.create() no longer resolves and isHealthy() no longer reports true when a probe stream ends without an exit code (#2807)

Python

  • Caller handler exceptions in the code-interpreter SDK propagate as SandboxException instead of being logged and swallowed mid-stream (#2697)
  • Legacy SSE normalization runs in linear time; large unterminated events and long leading whitespace no longer cause quadratic CPU work (#2845)

JavaScript

  • SandboxManager.renewSandbox returns the renew response, so callers can see the expiresAt the server actually applied; source-compatible with existing await call sites (#2699)

Kotlin

  • The first SSE event survives a leading UTF-8 BOM, so Execution.id is no longer null on execd streams that start with one (#2800)

C#

  • Endpoint cache invalidation is scoped to the in-flight key: pausing or killing one sandbox no longer discards another sandbox's just-fetched endpoint (#2843)

Go

  • WatchMetrics delivers metric snapshots as they arrive instead of buffering until the stream ends and failing to parse (#2805)

Controller

  • The Helm chart's manager ClusterRole gains pods/exec: create, fixing the Restart recycle strategy on Helm installs — every restart exec was previously Forbidden, so pods returned to a Restart pool were never recycled; a sync test now asserts the chart never drifts from the generated role (#2780)

Execd

  • The /proxy route reuses one shared upstream connection pool instead of dialing per request and leaking each connection for 600 seconds, so steady proxy traffic no longer accumulates sockets in execd and the sandboxed server (#2788)
  • Code contexts fail fast: an unusable working directory returns 400 immediately instead of retrying for five minutes and answering 500 (#2782); a context whose Jupyter session is already gone (for example after a Jupyter restart) deletes cleanly instead of failing forever and blocking language-wide deletes (#2785); listing contexts for a non-kernel language returns 400 instead of 500 (#2792)
  • Path handling: $ characters that name no variable (for example Outer$1.class) stay literal instead of silently expanding to another path (#2779); invalid isolated-session search globs return 400 like host search (#2760); file birth time is only used when the returned inode and device match the queried entry (#2612)

Networking

egress

  • [EXPERIMENTAL] The credential-bound Fast Sandbox roadmap advances on four fronts: admitted HTTP/1.1 requests are served against immutable subject dispatch snapshots with handshake-registry pinning and response-header redaction, and HTTP/2 negotiation is disabled for subject TLS (#2794); existing decrypted connections are fenced and drained on binding-removal transitions using OPENSANDBOX_EGRESS_REVISION_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (#2836); subject transports are torn down on Unload, suspend, receiver failure, and shutdown, refusing source-IP reuse while old connections remain unconfirmed (#2841); and bounded transition counters and latency histograms distinguish confirmed results from pending reconciliation without leaking subject identities (#2838). The feature remains off by default; all and unset behavior is unchanged.
  • DNS replies to non-EDNS UDP clients are kept within 512 bytes with TC set so legacy resolvers retry over TCP, instead of receiving oversized answers with an unsolicited OPT record (#2802)
  • Invalid ports in OPENSANDBOX_EGRESS_DNS_UPSTREAM entries fail at startup like a hostname does, instead of starting normally and answering SERVFAIL for every forwarded query (#2809)

ingress

  • A relayed WebSocket handshake rejection no longer truncates the backend's error body: the stale Content-Length is dropped so rejections larger than 1 KiB arrive intact (#2798)
  • Route port segments with a leading sign (+8080, +08080) are rejected in header and URI modes instead of silently routing to the unsigned port (#2806)

Fast Sandbox

  • Fastlet Proxy CPU/memory requests and limits are configurable through controller.fastletProxy.resources, wired to four new controller flags with quantity validation; prior fixed defaults are preserved (#2870 fast-sandbox#215)
  • RootfsOnly snapshot qualification now derives its digests from the deployed Firecracker bundle instead of requiring operator-provisioned profiles, with hardened qualification startup and diagnostics (#2709 fast-sandbox#185)
  • FSEP-0003 proposes always-on Fastlet control-plane authentication (ServiceAccount tokens with a controller-injected allow list); the design draft lands with this pin and carries no code — no behavior changes in this release (#2870 fast-sandbox#206)

Misc

  • OSEPs: OSEP-0027 drafts an optional, path-scoped E2B compatibility adapter for core agent workflows on Linux/amd64 Fast Sandbox; the proposal remains draft with unvalidated candidate versions (#2591)
  • CLI: osb config set validates keys and values at set time instead of failing every later command with SDK internals (#2766); a bad credential vault payload shows the parser error instead of a generic "failed to read" (#2744); the deprecated osb devops group is removed in favor of osb diagnostics (#2823)
  • Console: node-agent readyz probes bracket IPv6 pod IPs so IPv6-primary clusters no longer report the DaemonSet critical (#2799); events.k8s.io events show their timestamps on the K8s Events page (#2803); a tenant-filtered K8s view no longer mixes in system pods and events (#2808)
  • Node-agent chart: the health port is derived correctly from a host:port serverAddr, which previously rendered containerPort: 0 and blocked installation (#2789)
  • CI and tests: the execd-init container-contract tests join the gating python e2e suite instead of a non-blocking dedicated job (#2829); the fast-sandbox lane runs storage-independent scenarios once on the overlaybd lane, projected to cut the job from ~40 to ~28 minutes (#2831); the OSEP-0018 hardening floor is wired and verified on that lane, establishing that the current fsb guest kernel has no Landlock and the floor degrades per its fail-open contract (#2833); comment cleanup across cross-language e2e suites and scripts, including removal of a dead integration entry (#2821 #2822); a gin test-mode race in execd controller tests is fixed (#2842)

Upgrade & Compatibility

  • execd-as-init default: [runtime] execd_run_as_init now defaults to true — the server injects EXECD_INIT=1 and execd owns the sandbox process tree. Deployments relying on the classic topology set execd_run_as_init = false; fsb golden-image templates keep their baked topology until rebuilt (#2825)
  • DevOps routes removed: GET /sandboxes/{id}/diagnostics/inspect, diagnostics/summary, and the scope-less plain-text fallback on diagnostics/logs/events (including legacy tail/since/container/limit parameters) are gone; scope is required and its omission returns 422. The stable scoped Diagnostics API is unchanged, and its only known consumer was the removed CLI group (#2826 #2823)
  • CLI migrations: osb devops logs|events|inspect|summary are removed — use osb diagnostics logs <id> --scope container -o raw, osb diagnostics events <id> --scope runtime -o raw, osb sandbox get <id> -o json, and osb diagnostics context <id> (#2823); osb config set now rejects unknown keys and invalid values at set time (#2766)
  • Snapshot mode: the default remains full; rootfsOnly requires the fast-sandbox backend with OCI-backed sandboxes, and Docker/Kubernetes return 409 UNSUPPORTED_RUNTIME. A rootfs-only restore is an explicit create(snapshotId=...) cold boot — processes and RAM are discarded, the entrypoint re-runs, and resume moves from milliseconds to seconds; pause/resume checkpoints stay full-only (#2709 #2835)
  • Fastlet Proxy resources: the new controller.fastletProxy.resources chart value carries CPU/memory requests and limits into the Fastlet Pod spec and the ResourceAware memory budget; defaults are unchanged, so no action is required unless you want to tune them (#2870 fast-sandbox#215)
  • Code-interpreter readiness: probes require a confirmed zero exit, so environments where the probe previously "passed" with an unknown exit code will now surface SandboxReadyTimeoutException/unhealthy — investigate the runtime instead of retrying blindly (#2807)
  • Python handler errors: code-interpreter ExecutionHandlers that raise now abort the stream with a SandboxException instead of the run completing silently (#2697)
  • Pool validation: capacitySpec.bufferMin above bufferMax returns 422 on create and update; pools already applied with the invalid shape still list and load, but should be corrected (#2801)
  • Error code normalization: reserved-metadata PATCH rejections return SANDBOX::INVALID_METADATA_LABEL on all backends — clients matching the bare INVALID_METADATA_LABEL literal must update (#2793 #2796)
  • Docker configuration: docker.pids_limit = 0 now disables the limit (previously rejected by validation) (#2786); with [docker].publish_host set, the server reaches published sandbox ports at that address, which changes proxy/sidecar connectivity for deployments that pinned it (#2846)
  • Egress DNS upstream validation: OPENSANDBOX_EGRESS_DNS_UPSTREAM entries with an invalid port now fail sidecar startup; fix previously "accepted" values like 8.8.8.8:0 or 8.8.8.8:70000 before upgrading (#2809)
  • Request validation: template-list metadata filters with malformed segments return 400 INVALID_METADATA_FORMAT instead of a silently empty page; env= still filters on the empty value (#2790); subPath values with Windows-separator traversal are rejected on all runtimes (#2749)
  • Images: opensandbox/<component>:release-1.3.0-rc.1 (all three registries; fsb images for fast-sandbox)
  • Packages: unchanged — SDK/CLI artifacts publish at the 1.3.0 stable release
  • Charts: render from this tag (helm template ./manifests/charts/opensandbox)
  • Kubernetes: supported range v1.21 – v1.34
  • Skew: server ↔ CLI/SDK same line supported; ±1 minor warns

entry.title: OpenSandbox 1.2.1
entry.content:
Stable patch release for users upgrading from 1.2.0, including both 1.2.1 release candidates and subsequent fixes. Server, CLI, SDKs, charts, and platform images ship together at 1.2.1.

Highlights

  • Dynamic credentials: Credential Vault Exchange resolves credentials per request across the server, egress, and all five SDKs, without vault persistence of resolved secrets (#2457 #2535 #2534 #2560).
  • Multi-version Fast Sandbox VMMs: managed Firecracker 1.16.1/1.17.0 bundles let new template builds select the highest installed version while existing artifacts restore with their exact recorded VMM version, failing explicitly if it is unavailable (#2795 #2812 fast-sandbox#189).
  • Safer data and capacity management: staged uploads reduce overwrite data loss where atomic replacement is available, controller restarts preserve live-sandbox Pods, and Docker enforces requested writable-layer disk quotas (#2433 #2478 #2398 #2716).

Server

  • Carry template CPU/memory shapes through creation and snapshot restore on ResourceAware pools; legacy pools retain their existing behavior (#2602 #2619 #2623 #2628 #2633).
  • Enforce Docker resourceLimits.disk on the writable container layer, returning 400 for unsupported drivers or invalid limits instead of silently ignoring them (#2716).
  • Allow Docker snapshots directly from paused sandboxes (#1941).
  • Move the server-proxied data path into maintenance mode; existing traffic remains supported, but deployments should migrate to the ingress gateway (#2548).
  • Reject unknown fields in closed request objects rather than silently accepting misspelled options (#2576).
  • Reduce Kubernetes API traffic and list costs through per-object informer invalidation and server-side metadata selectors (#2599 #2559).
  • Require OCI template artifacts to be SHA-256-pinned in the expected repository (#2491).
  • Fail startup when Docker expiration enforcement cannot be restored, except for concurrently removed containers (#2533).
  • Other fixes improve create-timeout diagnostics and idle-pause probe bounds (#2434 #2596); Docker mount, host-path, and resource validation (#2421 #2505 #2474 #2701 #2751); proxy GET bodies and exhaustion errors (#2518 #2519); and empty metadata filters, name validation, and API error codes (#2461 #2499 #2702 #2703).

SDKs

  • All five SDKs support exchange credential sources and credential-only binding auth; Kotlin/C# consumers must recompile and review widened credential types (#2534 #2560).
  • Optional detailed download APIs expose status, headers, ranges, and partial-response detection without requiring changes to existing adapters; Python/JavaScript/C# report unknown totals when encoded lengths cannot describe decoded output (#1597 #2592).
  • Documentation expands lifecycle/network options, exchange credentials, template workflows, and S3 examples (#2590 #2597 #2620 #2506).

Python

  • MCP adds command_get_status and command_get_logs for background-command polling and incremental output (#2648).
  • Silent command SSE streams now time out; abandoned downloads release connections, and streaming failures consistently use SDK exceptions (#2527 #2487 #2531 #2570 #2515 #2525).
  • Graceful pool shutdown drains cleanup kills rather than abandoning sandboxes; smaller fixes cover endpoint invalidation, adapter redirects/hooks, and actionable MCP errors (#2507 #2409 #2553 #2524).

JavaScript

  • Prevent positive sub-millisecond command timeouts from becoming unbounded; fix unlimited redirect deadlines, structured isolated-session errors, and closing downloads during iteration (#2440 #2488 #2466 #2514).

Kotlin

  • Round fractional command/session timeout milliseconds upward, preventing sub-millisecond values from becoming unbounded (#2537).

C#

  • Use the common CredentialSource model for inline and exchange variants; update inline-only assumptions when recompiling (#2560).

Go

  • Preserve code-interpreter output fragments in Execution.Text() without inserting newlines (#2447).
  • Enforce wake, Running-state, and interpreter-readiness budgets without truncating established streams or accepting unfinished readiness probes (#2572 #2611 #2528 #2668 #2480 #2504).
  • Preserve cleanup ownership during cancelled pool operations and fence incomplete destruction for retry; cancelled acquires no longer consume healthy idle capacity (#2542 #2617 #2580 #2616).
  • Fence stale endpoint lookups after lifecycle changes without cancelling fetches still needed by other callers (#2503 #2564 #2579).
  • Other fixes bound retry overflow and server-supplied delays (#2452 #2508 #2509); improve SSE parsing, multipart boundaries, and header merging (#2439 #2618 #2468 #2529); and correct pool maintenance, telemetry deadlines, and timeout tests (#2453 #2565 #2540 #2479).

Controller

  • Add namespace-scoped caches, configurable leader-election timings, and controller.extraArgs for deployment tuning (#2571 #2651 #2566).
  • Recover pool allocations before eviction, protecting live-sandbox Pods after controller restarts (#2398).
  • Reject rootfs snapshots missing required digests and retain their Pods instead of deleting the only resumable runtime (#2482).
  • Other fixes prevent lifecycle-related memory growth, remove excess idle Pods after poolMax reductions, and place the recovery ConfigMap in the correct namespace (#2646 #2470 #2694).

Execd

  • Discover Jupyter runtime tokens when JUPYTER_TOKEN is unset (#2448).
  • Stage uploads and isolated-file replacements before rename to protect existing content; atomicity requires a writable containing directory, with an in-place permission fallback described below (#2433 #2478).
  • Preserve isolated-workspace contents and modes during copy-up/rename, honor overlay deletions, and reject symlink chmod rather than following host targets (#2638 #2469).
  • Refresh MITM trust after Kubernetes egress-sidecar CA rotation, avoiding persistent TLS failures (#2582).
  • Isolated runs no longer consume shell control input; deleting Bash sessions terminates all active runs, and PTY close hangs up ordinary background jobs while retaining terminal-like behavior for HUP-ignoring jobs (#2517 #2731 #2733).
  • Restore Jupyter startup retries and session cleanup, fail unsupported languages promptly, and deliver output/errors before reporting completion (#2486 #2689 #2606).
  • Recover SQL execution after temporary setup failures without automatically replaying queries (#2757).
  • Security hardening: percent-encode control bytes in download headers and correct RFC 8187 filename encoding (#2741 #2516).
  • Other fixes cover command-log correlation and validation (#2598 #2686); PTY output and exported escapes (#2644 #2772); download/search validation and file timestamps (#2451 #2687 #2604); cgroup-v1 metrics and SQL byte rendering (#2641 #2685); and an opt-in legacy SSE workaround for older Kotlin/JVM deployments (#2472).

Networking

egress

  • Credential Vault Exchange: resolve fresh headers through UDS/HTTPS using egress-derived sandbox identity and request targets; resolution fails closed, and resolved secrets are neither persisted nor cached by the vault (#2457 #2495 #2500 #2501 #2535 #2538 #2539 #2547 #2549 #2563).
  • Enforce Fast Sandbox per-subject TCP port and IP/CIDR-plus-port policies, including original-destination checks through MITM (#2662).
  • Hot-reload Fast Sandbox operator deny/allow rules and reachable-port caps without restarting egress; changes apply atomically across active subjects, retaining the previous policy on failure and rejecting stale DNS answers after revocation. The network-security guide documents deployment, precedence, and enforcement boundaries while preserving old guide URLs (#2727 #2814).
  • Allow dns+nft sidecar policy PATCH/DELETE to opt into blocking established traffic with dropEstablished=true; Fast Sandbox is not supported (#2346).
  • [EXPERIMENTAL] Harden strict Actions v2 ownership/persistence and subject readiness with durable fences, authenticated child sessions, and acknowledged policy/Vault snapshots; defaults remain unchanged (#2441 #2460 #2493 #2586 #2589 #2609 #2634 #2649 #2666 #2708).
  • [EXPERIMENTAL] — not for production: OPENSANDBOX_EGRESS_FSB_INTERCEPTION_MODE=credential-bound selects a budgeted TLS handshake experiment, not working credential injection or request forwarding: all decrypted HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 origin traffic is still denied. all remains the default; the OSEP-0023 rollout describes unfinished work (#2737 #2797 #2777).
  • Security fixes: policy PATCH preserves untouched deny rules, and invalid defaultAction values are rejected rather than producing inconsistent, potentially fail-open enforcement (#2664 #2662 #2693).
  • Renew Fast Sandbox DNS leases in the kernel and preserve other subjects' leases during deletion (#2652 #2653).
  • Other hardening covers experimental interception-port validation, idempotent readiness hooks, and nft smoke/read-back checks (#2587 #2510 #2543 #2735).

ingress

  • Use one queue-plus-wait wake budget and validate it against flight lifetime; mixed regular/Fast Sandbox wake routing no longer panics at startup (#2511 #2513 #2600).
  • Other fixes validate legacy hostname ports, correct final-status/client-IP telemetry, and remove a wake-test race (#2578 #2484 #2688 #2512).

Fast Sandbox

  • Bundle managed Firecracker 1.16.1/1.17.0 binaries for runtime and template builds, selecting the exact artifact-recorded version for restore rather than silently using the latest installed VMM (#2795 #2812 fast-sandbox#189).
  • Isolate ResourceAware direct-Firecracker VMMs in a bounded cgroup subtree, protecting Fastlet from pool-local OOM while retaining failed-runtime identities for cleanup (#2626 fast-sandbox#162).
  • Enable free-page reporting in new object-store templates, returning guest-freed memory to the host without changing static resource commitments; OCI templates are not yet supported (#2546 fast-sandbox#114).
  • Improve OCI storage with reusable warm ublk devices and best-effort checkpoint/rootfs layer compaction (#2594 fast-sandbox#163 #2546 fast-sandbox#158).
  • Reuse locally published OCI checkpoint blobs for faster same-node resume, with bounded storage, protection for live-device references, and registry fallback (#2812 fast-sandbox#178).
  • [EXPERIMENTAL] RootfsOnly OCI snapshots now extend from runtime capture to Fast Sandbox's FastPath and SandboxSnapshot CRD, with capability checks, produced-mode validation, and journaled recovery. Restores cold-boot without preserving memory; OpenSandbox REST/SDK mode selection and RootfsOnly pause/resume remain unsupported (#2706 fast-sandbox#173 #2812 fast-sandbox#177).
  • OverlayBD template builds now inject guest-control and validate freeze/thaw by default; existing templates need rebuilding to gain RootfsOnly capture capability (#2812 fast-sandbox#183).
  • Add shared YAML-configured file logging and rotation for first-party Kubernetes components, with optional stderr mirroring; log collectors and custom launch flags need migration (#2812 fast-sandbox#197).
  • Expose timestamped template-build phases, elapsed times, and failures across image pull, rootfs preparation, guest readiness, snapshotting, and publication (#2815 fast-sandbox#201).
  • [EXPERIMENTAL] Fence delayed strict Actions v2 operations with durable owner identity and confirmed retirement; v1 remains the default (#2546 fast-sandbox#152).
  • Add namespace/API-client tuning, chart scheduling hooks, optional direct-origin delivery, and template-baked execd init mode (#2581 fast-sandbox#161 #2566 #2494 #2497).
  • Immediate create/pause/resume transitions now converge without settle delays, and active pools replace terminal Fastlet Pods instead of counting them as capacity (#2626 fast-sandbox#166 #2706 fast-sandbox#172).
  • Recover idle shared snapfiles attachments after ublkd device loss without manual cache wipes; attachments with other Sandbox leases remain protected rather than being rebuilt under live consumers (#2812 fast-sandbox#193).
  • Other fixes cover BusyBox-based template readiness, timestamp precision, and existing-secret rendering (#2626 fast-sandbox#164 #2706 fast-sandbox#170 #2695); restore cache-affinity matching for Firecracker image/template references (#2812 fast-sandbox#119).
  • Expand ResourceAware rollout coverage and correct fixture CPU budgets without changing saturation capacity (#2622 #2637 #2647 #2669 #2812); improve ublk recovery, exchange/console integration tests, KVM selection, and snapshot-staging documentation (#2454 #2561 #2676 #2665 #2714); gate PR KVM runs on maintainer-added ok-to-test, without unrelated labels cancelling an active run (#2813).

Misc

  • Console: add a browser PTY shell with BFF-held credentials and automatic session cleanup, improve disconnect feedback, and translate the interface into English (#2233 #2639 #2657).
  • Node-agent: collect guest kernel/init console output through an opt-in vm-console source, using node-local VM metadata and restart-safe offsets rather than cluster-wide Sandbox watches (#2234 #2677 #2546 fast-sandbox#154).
  • CLI fixes preserve literal output and string configuration (#2520 #2522); improve config, argument, timeout, and overwrite-refusal errors (#2521 #2551 #2692 #2742 #2748 #2743); and repair PTY cleanup, metrics watching, and table output, including osb template get's missing manifest_ref (#2523 #2691 #2747 #2745).
  • Examples add an ACK PeerPods/TDX walkthrough and adopt Google ADK 2.13.0's native environment/toolset, while correcting the Python network-isolation example (#2545 #2734 #2711).
  • Governance/docs publish the AAIF charter and DCO/CC-BY-4.0 contribution rules, clarify voting and ownership, reconcile proposal statuses, and document signing/provenance gaps (#2490 #2678 #2679 #2680 #2624 #2670 #2671 #2672 #2673 #2674 #2467).
  • Maintenance covers orphan node-agent streams, dead-code/test cleanup, single-platform Kind imports, and Linux/eBPF test setup (#2471 #2496 #2640 #2736 #2573 #2473).
  • Release preparation includes candidate version bumps, notes, and generated BOMs (#2583 #2584 #2585 #2588 #2720 #2723 #2724 #2725 #2726).

Upgrade & Compatibility

  • Managed Firecracker: deploy matching charts, runtime, and builder images; runtimeEnvironments → firecracker.firecracker.vmmDir is now supported and must reference an absolute managed-binary directory. New managed builds choose the highest installed version (currently 1.17.0); Full/RootfsOnly restores require the manifest-recorded version and fail if it is unavailable, rather than falling back to latest. Keep 1.16.1 binaries for existing artifacts without relabeling them; retaining old binaries does not guarantee downgrade compatibility for persisted Fast Sandbox state (#2795 #2812 fast-sandbox#189).
  • Request validation: remove unknown keys from closed request objects and use only one alias spelling; these now return 422. Replace ImageAuth.token/Docker-config extras with supported username/password, remove trailing newlines from names/addresses, and use only allow/deny for policy defaultAction (#2576 #2499 #2693).
  • SDK credential models: Kotlin/C# are not ABI-compatible with 1.2.0; recompile and review widened sources and nullable/typeless auth assumptions. Exchange auth contains only credential; Python inline sources reject extra keys, and generated-model users should prefer handwritten models. Use keyed Go literals for changed source/metadata models and Execution; JSON round-tripping loses Execution.Text()'s private formatting mode (#2560 #2534 #2447).
  • Proxy/ingress: migrate maintenance-only server-proxy options to ingress; legacy hostname ports must be canonical decimals in 1–65535, and --wake-park-budget must be below --wake-max-flight-lifetime (#2548 #2578 #2511).
  • Docker quotas: supplied disk/storage/ephemeral-storage limits must be positive and supported by the storage driver or creation returns 400. Only the writable layer is covered, not bind mounts, volumes, or image layers; Windows retains its existing disk-size behavior (#2716).
  • Docker preflight/startup: correct duplicate, root, colon-containing, or reserved mount destinations and quantities above signed int64; an explicit / host-path allowlist authorizes all POSIX descendants. Expiration-restore failures now prevent startup unless the container was concurrently removed; investigate persistent daemon errors (#2421 #2505 #2751 #2474 #2533).
  • Downloads: detailed APIs remain optional for custom adapters; check 206/isPartial and ranges before appending, and close response bodies. Unknown totals use -1; encoded HTTP lengths/ranges are not decoded progress or resume offsets. Python callers should catch SDK exceptions rather than raw httpx errors (#1597 #2592 #2515 #2525).
  • Timeouts and polling: Python command streams time out after max(request_timeout, 30s) without bytes; raise request_timeout for legitimate silence. MCP pollers must read logs once more after completion and retain opaque cursors; empty output is not completion. Custom Go pool stores must honor cancellation, and incomplete destruction stays fenced for retry (#2527 #2648 #2580).
  • Upload atomicity: use writable containing directories for staged uploads/isolated replacements; existing writable files fall back to non-atomic truncation on staging permission errors. Ordinary /files/replace remains in-place. Staged replacement preserves modes, not xattrs/ACLs/capabilities/SELinux labels; ownership is best effort for ordinary writes and session UID/GID for isolated writes (#2433 #2478).
  • Upload storage: hardlinks/open readers retain the old inode, multipart overwrites may need roughly three times the file size, and interrupted writers can leave staging files. Avoid reserved .osb-upload-/.osb-staging- names, especially a prefix plus 16 hex digits; rename existing collisions directly. Special-file targets are rejected, while bind-mounted/open files can prevent rename; directory sync is best effort (#2433 #2478).
  • Session lifecycle: isolated foreground stdin is now /dev/null; use files or here-documents. Bash-session deletion terminates all overlapping runs; PTY close adds SIGHUP and up to 500 ms before group kill, while nohup/HUP-ignoring jobs can survive (#2517 #2731 #2733).
  • Jupyter/JVM: custom images need an explicit token or discoverable runtime token files and the requested kernel. Prefer shaded sandbox-api 1.0.18+ over EXECD_SSE_LEGACY_COMPAT, which is off by default and removes structured exit_code values (#2448 #2689 #2472).
  • Controller configuration: cache scope must include all managed namespaces, plus Fast Sandbox template/runtime-environment namespaces; it does not change RBAC or provide tenant isolation. Review controller.podRecovery.*, which now takes effect, and remove obsolete ConfigMaps left by plain-manifest upgrades. Custom election timings require lease > renew > 1.2×retry (#2571 #2581 fast-sandbox#161 #2694 #2651).
  • Exchange deployment: align server/SDK/egress versions; the sidecar live revision runtime does not support exchange. Resolver caller authentication is not implemented—Ed25519/JWKS remains design-only. Use a protected UDS or trusted-egress-only HTTPS with trusted CAs; sandbox allow rules must not expose resolvers, and MITM UID exclusion alone is not isolation (#2501 #2549 #2631 #2547).
  • [EXPERIMENTAL] Strict Actions v2: enable matching OPENSANDBOX_EGRESS_ACTIONS_API_VERSION/Fastlet actionsApiVersion values of sandbox.fast.io/actions/v2 only on clean-base direct-Firecracker deployments with durable state, isolated management ports, and manager authorization. Pause/resume, snapshots/restore, live binding removal, owner migration, and same-UID reuse remain unsupported; use terminal deletion/new UIDs, preserve fences, and never treat fencing as authentication or downgrade existing state to v1 (#2441 #2460 #2493 #2546 fast-sandbox#152).
  • [EXPERIMENTAL] Credential-bound interception: OPENSANDBOX_EGRESS_FSB_INTERCEPTION_MODE=credential-bound still denies decrypted application forwarding and must not be enabled in production. With the switch unset, both legacy gates enabled remain a deprecated alias; revision-runtime alone is installation-only. Explicit mode/gate conflicts, empty/unknown values, and setting this switch on sidecar fail startup (#2737 #2797).
  • Experimental startup requirements: credential-bound mode requires transparent MITM, dns+nft, and only default interception ports 80,443; remove insecure TLS verification, chained proxies, and effective ignore_hosts/allow_hosts. Runtime-user config.yaml then config.yml are checked; read/parse errors fail closed. To return to all, unset both legacy gates; sidecar live revision also rejects extra interception ports (#2587 #2797).
  • Port policies: Fast Sandbox supports TCP only, at most 256 ports per rule, and no domain-plus-port combinations; normal updates preserve established flows. dropEstablished is supported only on dns+nft sidecar PATCH/DELETE, ignored by POST, and unsupported in Fast Sandbox, dns-only, live-revision, or chained-proxy-plus-transparent-MITM modes; it installs packet drops, not TCP resets. Removing a port-only allow alone does not trigger established-flow blocking (#2662 #2346).
  • Operator-rule reload: Fast Sandbox reloads runtime-mutable rule files on a one-minute tick; mount ConfigMaps as directories, not subPath, and allow for kubelet projection delay. Image-baked rules still require a new image and recreation. Successful reloads clear DNS-learned leases, so allowed domains need another lookup; failed reloads retain the previous overlay, and established connections are not forcibly terminated (#2727 #2814).
  • Network-security boundaries: domain denies filter DNS, not direct connections to known IPs; use explicit IP/CIDR denies or default-deny policies for those paths. Operator denies override operator allows, so permitted internal services require a deny-range carve-out. Classic Docker/Kubernetes creation injects egress only when networkPolicy is supplied; poolRef plus networkPolicy is unsupported, so configure pooled controls in the template (#2814).
  • ResourceAware rollout: direct-Firecracker resource-admission.json moves from v2 to v3; old/new Fastlets reject the other configuration version, so coordinate controller/Fastlet upgrades per pool. Heartbeats remain v2. Hosts require writable cgroup v2, clone3(CLONE_INTO_CGROUP), and zero effective pool swap; the shared memory ceiling is not per-VM protection or a guarantee of survival across container replacement (#2626 fast-sandbox#162).
  • Restore sizing: ResourceAware pools use template CPU/memory shapes; new snapshots replay source limits, which restore-time caller limits must match. Legacy pools and snapshots without recorded limits retain their prior behavior (#2623 #2628 #2633).
  • [EXPERIMENTAL] RootfsOnly: Full remains the default; explicit RootfsOnly mode is available through Fast Sandbox FastPath/CRDs for reusable OCI snapshots, not pause/resume or OpenSandbox REST/SDK mode selection. New capture requires qualified patched Firecracker 1.17.0 templates, a live guest helper, qualified kernel/OverlayBD backend, exclusive ext4 ownership, and an absolute FAST_SANDBOX_ROOTFS_QUALIFICATION profile with matching digests/storage attestation; custom binary digests do not bypass the version gate. Upgrade runtime, Fastlet/Proxy, builder, and tools together, rebuild qualified templates, and preserve journals/fences. Restore cold-boots and reruns the entrypoint; no application-memory preservation or validated cross-CPU/architecture portability is promised (#2706 fast-sandbox#173 #2812 fast-sandbox#177 fast-sandbox#189).
  • OverlayBD template builds: guest-control injection and freeze/thaw validation are now mandatory for the OCI builder; FSB_GUEST_CONTROL_ENABLED is no longer an opt-out. Missing/incompatible helpers or failed probes stop the build. Native templates are unchanged; existing OCI templates need rebuilding rather than metadata edits to gain capture capability (#2812 fast-sandbox#183).
  • Fast Sandbox logs: covered Kubernetes components now write rotating files under /var/log/fast-sandbox by default (100 MiB per file, 10 backups, 7-day backup retention, gzip); application logs no longer appear in kubectl logs unless alsoStderr: true is configured. Replace legacy klog output flags with the shared logging YAML, wire ConfigMap/log-volume mounts for chart-managed static workloads, and configure each tenant namespace separately. Configuration is startup-only: use controlled Pool draining/replacement for Fastlets, not deletion of live Pods, and arrange collection before ephemeral logs are lost. Explicit missing/invalid configuration or unwritable output prevents startup; rotation limits are not a hard disk quota and do not cover guest/VM logs (#2812 fast-sandbox#197).
  • OCI checkpoint cache: reserve space for the additional blob cache (defaults: 16 GiB, 4096 files, 1 GiB free-space reserve), separately from OverlayBD's block cache. Keep staging/cache/device state on one filesystem for hard-link reuse; cross-filesystem placement or contention falls back to the registry. Set FAST_SANDBOX_OCI_BLOB_CACHE_SIZE_BYTES=0 to disable blob-cache insertion/lookups; active-device pins remain protected, including when budgets shrink (#2812 fast-sandbox#178).
  • ublkd recovery: automatic shared-snapfiles rebuilding applies only when no other Sandbox lease needs the attachment; it is not transparent recovery of running VMs. Remove affected Sandboxes through their normal lifecycle before retrying when other leases remain, rather than manually wiping shared caches (#2812 fast-sandbox#193).
  • Template rebuilds: opt-in runtime.execd_run_as_init needs rebuilt templates; execd remains a subreaper beneath guest PID 1. Free-page reporting also needs rebuilt object-store templates and compatible VMM/kernel support, cannot toggle restored device state, and does not enable OCI reporting or justify higher overcommit; rollback uses an older template (#2494 #2497 #2546 fast-sandbox#114).
  • OCI chart defaults: idle ublk devices are now reserved; set runtime.oci.poolLow=0 for on-demand allocation and match poolSizeGB to rounded-up rootfs capacity. P2P remains enabled by default; custom runtime.config needs separate adjustment for direct-origin delivery (#2594 fast-sandbox#163 #2566).
  • Snapshot integrity: missing commit digests now fail pause while retaining Pods; old snapshots are not repaired. OCI template references must carry a full SHA-256 digest in the expected repository; rebuild invalid references (#2482 #2491).
  • CLI scripts: non-positive request timeouts and empty rule targets are usage errors; osb config init overwrite refusal now exits 1 without changing the file (#2742 #2692 #2743).
  • VM console collection: opt in to vm-console, align hostPaths.vmConsole with the runtime state root, cover every runtime node, and manage file-sink retention (#2234 #2677).
  • Artifact verification: umbrella workflows do not provide blanket signing/provenance coverage; BOM digest matching is not proof of origin, and signature requirements must not be bypassed (#2467).

entry.title: OpenSandbox 1.2.1-rc.2
entry.content:
Second release candidate on the 1.2.1 patch line, carrying everything merged since release-1.2.1-rc.1 (2026-11-04). The headline is OSEP-0026 resource-aware oversubscription landing end to end: the server records each template's effective machine shape, forwards it as per-sandbox limits on ResourceAware pools, and replays recorded limits across snapshot restores, validated by a dedicated KVM verify lane. Fast Sandbox networking reaches parity on port-scoped egress rules, the experimental OSEP-0023 subject revision runtime advances from session foundations to an enforced readiness gate, and the pinned fast-sandbox gains opt-in rootfs-only OCI snapshots. A safety batch closes real data-loss and availability bugs: unknown fields in closed request objects are now rejected, a controller restart can no longer evict pods of live sandboxes, and the server-proxied data path enters maintenance mode. Images publish now; SDK/CLI packages ship at the 1.2.1 stable bump.

Highlights

  • Resource-aware oversubscription (OSEP-0026) lands end to end: template machine shapes are recorded at build time, forwarded as per-sandbox limits when the selected pool reports ResourceAware, snapshot restores replay the source's recorded limits instead of failing, and a verify-resourceaware CI stage asserts the chain down to cgroup values (#2602 #2623 #2628 #2633 #2637)
  • Fast Sandbox egress parity and hardening: port-scoped NetworkRule.ports rules are now enforced per subject (the 400 rejection is lifted) (#2662); DNS leases renew in the kernel and survive neighbour removal (#2652 #2653); the experimental OSEP-0023 subject revision runtime reaches a readiness gate on acknowledged snapshots (#2666)
  • Safety and lifecycle: closed request objects reject unknown fields with 422 instead of silently ignoring them (#2576); a controller restart no longer evicts pods allocated to live sandboxes (#2398); the server-proxy data path is deprecated into maintenance mode — route sandbox traffic through the ingress gateway (#2548)

Server

  • Resource-aware oversubscription (OSEP-0026): each template's effective machine shape (post-default CPU/memory) is recorded in spec_json.machine at build time and projected identically into the CRD (#2623); template-mode creates forward it as per-sandbox resources.limits when — and only when — the selected pool reports ResourceAware, with LegacySlot/older FastPath pools failing safe to field-omitted and the pool-mode read TTL-cached (#2628); snapshot creation records the source's per-sandbox limits and restores replay them — previously a shaped template sandbox restored on a ResourceAware pool fell back to pool defaults and FastPath rejected the restore outright (#2633); FastPath stubs are regenerated with the resource-aware proto fields as groundwork (#2619); the contract is defined in OSEP-0026 (#2602)
  • The server-proxied data path is deprecated into maintenance mode: /sandboxes/{id}/proxy/{port}, the use_server_proxy parameter, the matching SDK options, and the CLI/MCP flags now carry explicit deprecation markers (Deprecation: true response header, runtime warnings per language), with security and bug fixes only — deployments should expose sandbox traffic through the ingress gateway (#2548)
  • Unknown fields in closed request objects are rejected with the sanitized 422 envelope instead of being silently discarded — readonly: true on a volume no longer silently stays writable, and createIfNotExist: false no longer leaves automatic volume creation enabled; ten models (image/auth/platform/volume/OSSFS/credential-proxy/snapshot-renew requests) now use extra = "forbid", and the TypeScript auth token property is deprecated (#2576)
  • The Kubernetes informer tracks writes per object instead of invalidating the whole cache: every create/patch/delete previously marked the entire workload cache unsynced until a full relist (up to 60 s), so a replica with steady writes (renewals are enough) served almost every read from the API server and ended in 429s; reads now go live only for the written object until the WATCH event confirms it (#2599)
  • The idle-pause activity probe honors its verdict contract: it never raises and every failure only drops the current candidate — a deeply nested 200 answer used to escape and skip the rest of the sweep; answers must now be uncompressed, fit 4 KiB, and arrive within timeoutSeconds as a whole-exchange bound (#2596)

SDKs

Code changes below ride the 1.2.1 stable release — rc ships no SDK packages.

Python

  • Malformed or out-of-range Content-Range integers are treated as unknown metadata (64-bit bounded), and async streaming responses are closed when response-metadata mapping fails in standard and isolated-session downloads — previously the underlying stream could stay open (#2570)
  • The Python MCP server exposes background command status and incremental logs: command_get_status (running state, exit code) and command_get_logs (content + opaque cursor), with polling guidance in the tool descriptions (#2648)

JavaScript

  • Positive sub-millisecond command timeouts round up to at least 1 ms — Math.round serialized 0.0004 s as timeout: 0, which disables the runtime bound for ordinary commands and selects the server default in Bash sessions (#2440)

Go

  • The wake budget bounds in-flight retries: after a marked wake 503, further attempts get a deadline for the remaining WakeOverallDeadline (headers only — established SSE streams and download bodies are never cut off) (#2572), and generic backoff or Retry-After waits that cannot fit the remaining budget are skipped so a mixed-failure retry no longer sleeps past the deadline or hides the ordinary error behind an older wake marker (#2611)
  • Pool hardening: a cancelled acquire no longer consumes a healthy idle entry or triggers a creation (#2616); graceful shutdown honors caller cancellation while waiting for independent acquires to drain (#2617); idle maintenance (shrink, near-expiry reaping) continues during creation backoff instead of being skipped for the whole tick (#2565)
  • An SSE response starting with a UTF-8 BOM no longer drops the first data frame or its event/id field — a command init frame could lose the execution ID (#2618); a running-timeout deadline expiring inside a status request now returns SandboxRunningTimeoutError regardless of timing, so errors.As classification is stable (#2668)

SDK READMEs catch up with the shipped surface: lifecycle idlePolicy + wake-retry, renewalPolicy, and port-scoped rules documented in all five languages (#2590); exchange credentials and fsb template create/poll flows documented for JavaScript, Python, Go (#2597) and Kotlin (#2620); the network isolation example uses the real imports and rule class (#2711)

Controller

  • Pool eviction after a controller restart no longer deletes pods of live sandboxes: the in-memory allocation store was only recovered inside Schedule, but eviction ran first on every pool reconcile — on the first reconcile after a restart every pod labelled for eviction looked idle and was deleted, including allocated ones; recovery now runs before any store read (#2398)
  • Lowering poolMax now scales idle pool pods in: it previously only capped growth, so idle pods above the new bound ran indefinitely; only idle pods are deleted, and already-planned deletions count toward the bound (#2470)
  • A deleted BatchSandbox's status-RV expectation is dropped, fixing unbounded leader heap growth — the entry for the last status patch of every BatchSandbox ever reconciled stayed for the life of the process (#2646)
  • Leader election timing is configurable: --leader-elect-lease-duration, --leader-elect-renew-deadline, and --leader-elect-retry-period (plus chart values), so operators on slower control planes can stop a 10 s API-server stall from forcing a full re-election; defaults are unchanged (#2651)
  • Chart: the controller feature-flags ConfigMap is rendered into the controller's namespace — it went to the Helm release namespace, where the controller never read it, so controller.podRecovery.* was silently ignored (#2694)

Execd

  • The isolated-session files API hides overlay-deleted entries: kernel whiteouts (0/0 devices), user.overlay.opaque directories, and the API's own .wh. markers now hide lower entries in stat/read/list/search — after rm f && mkdir d the deleted f and d/x were still readable with their old contents, and RemoveAll("d") left d/x listable until now (#2469)
  • Copy-up on rename and chmod is faithful to the lower layer: mode (including setuid/setgid/sticky) and session ownership are preserved, symlinks stay symlinks, lower-only directories can be renamed, and rm f.txt && mv f.txt g.txt no longer resurrects the deleted file; chmod refuses symlinks instead of following them to a host path (#2638)
  • MITM CA trust races against egress restarts are closed: bootstrap only trusts a CA that appeared after an observed absence or survived a stabilization window, and a lifetime watcher reinstalls system/merged/NSS/JDK trust whenever the exported CA content changes — previously a sidecar restart left the sandbox with the rotated-out CA everywhere until rebuild (#2582)
  • Foreground isolated runs no longer write their script to the shell's stdin: code that reads stdin (read, cat) consumed the rest of the script including the end marker, corrupting the exit code and hijacking the session; code now runs via eval with </dev/null, a syntax error ends the run with status 2 and the session survives (#2517)
  • Smaller fixes: the PTY holder's final output chunk is flushed before the exit frame instead of racing it (a background child holding the pipe delays exit by at most 2 s) (#2644); cgroup v1 metrics and OOM watch honor the container's mount root, so Docker-on-cgroup-v1 reported host CPU/memory instead of the sandbox's limits (#2641); directory downloads return 400 instead of a filesystem-dependent 500/empty-200, and a malformed Range header's 416 carries a message (#2451); an invalid /files/search glob returns 400 instead of 500 (or 200 on an empty directory) (#2687); created_at reports the inode birth time via statx, so chmod/rename no longer change it (#2604); Jupyter completion is derived from the kernel's actual outcome (reply + idle, IOPub errors retained) instead of racing it (#2606)

Networking

egress

  • Port-scoped egress rules are enforced per subject in fast sandbox: the per-subject nft path gained TCP port allow/drop chains (MITM matches the connection's original port, not the proxy listener), the fsb server passes ports through and merges by (target, ports), and the create-time 400 rejection is lifted — deny-before-allow and TCP-only semantics match the classic profile, and domain+ports stays rejected in both (#2662)
  • PATCH /policy on the classic sidecar no longer drops untouched rules: the shared merge key let an unrelated patch remove an existing deny and open blocked traffic (fail-open); base rules of scopes absent from the patch are now kept, matching the documented contract (#2664)
  • Fast-sandbox DNS leases renew in the kernel: the plain timed-element add succeeds but leaves the kernel expiry unchanged, so new connections to a cached IP were dropped once the first timeout lapsed; renewal now uses the add/delete/re-add sequence (#2652), and rebuilding the shared nft table when one subject is removed re-adds the remaining subjects' unexpired leases instead of leaving idle cached IPs blocked (#2653)
  • The experimental OSEP-0023 subject revision runtime advances [EXPERIMENTAL] (behind OPENSANDBOX_EGRESS_EXPERIMENTAL_REVISION_RUNTIME, admission still disabled): installation-only subject sessions with authenticated per-child IPC and fresh control generations (#2589), a FIFO lifecycle drain worker recording SET/REMOVE/rebind/takeover intents (#2609), per-subject decision snapshots installed after binding and after every Vault/policy mutation (#2634 #2649), and the data-plane-ready hook now gates on an acknowledged snapshot for the current fence/generation/digest — returning 503 while authority or the ACK is missing (#2666); the ownership and revision integration contract is pinned in OSEP-0022/0023 (#2586)
  • The experimental sidecar live revision runtime rejects extra interception ports at startup and fails closed on non-canonical (non-443) TLS destination ports, instead of letting them reach the later HTTP authority gate (#2587)

ingress

  • Wake policy reads reuse a single Kubernetes config: serving regular and fast-sandbox routes with wake enabled parsed REST config twice, and the second global flag registration panicked at startup with flag redefined: cluster (#2600)

Fast Sandbox

  • Native ublk warm pool on OCI deployments: OverlayBD now starts with a 4/8 pool of 2 GiB devices (chart-tunable runtime.oci.poolLow/poolHigh/poolSizeGB, poolLow=0 disables), so template creates hit pre-allocated devices instead of allocating on demand; CI asserts warm hits with no misses or daemon restarts (#2594 fast-sandbox#163)
  • Opt-in rootfs-only OCI snapshots (FSEP-0001) on the OverlayBD path: capture persists only the writable rootfs layer without a memory dump, and restore boots instead of resuming in place — smaller artifacts with no memory-sized staging window and no CPU-model pinning, with the artifact manifest driving restore; a failed RootfsOnly recovery suspends the route until recovery succeeds; runtime-level capability, the OpenSandbox snapshot API wiring comes later (#2706 fast-sandbox#173 fast-sandbox#167)
  • Lifecycle hardening: Fastlets are isolated from VM-pool OOM and retain drain errors, resource diagnostics, and failed runtime identities across readiness phases (#2626 fast-sandbox#162); immediate pause after create no longer races the controller's status projection — an interrupted pause keeps its intent and a concurrent resume preserves checkpoint lineage, so no client-side settle delay is needed (#2626 fast-sandbox#166)
  • Snapshot and reconciler recovery: quarantined captures are reconciled and unsafe routes withdrawn, exited quarantined runtimes retired, vsock paths isolated, suspended routes restored, and terminal Fastlet Pods are replaced only in active pools; reset revision timestamps preserve fractions (#2706 fast-sandbox#172 fast-sandbox#170)
  • Charts: the fast-sandbox controller and firecracker-runtime workloads accept podLabels/podAnnotations/nodeSelector/affinity, the runtime's DART P2P mesh can be disabled (runtime.p2p.enabled=false renders no headless Service/peer port and the agent pulls directly from the origin store), and the controller chart gains controller.extraArgs for unmodeled binary flags (#2566)
  • ResourceAware integration: a ResourceAware SandboxPool fixture with POOL_MODE=resource-aware selection (#2622), a verify-resourceaware stage asserting shaped-template forwarding at CR/cgroup/saturation levels (#2637), and the PR integration lane now runs the ResourceAware stack by default while nightly keeps LegacySlot coverage (#2647)
  • Smaller fix: the fast-sandbox chart skips the dev route-key Secret when routeKeys.existingSecret is set — production installs no longer render the published development-only Ed25519 private key (#2695)

Misc

  • Console: a browser sandbox shell bridges xterm to execd's PTY over a BFF WebSocket — entries on the tenant and admin lists, tenant keys and execd tokens stay on the BFF, one page open is one PTY (#2233); a dropped execd connection after connect reports as a lost shell instead of an error traceback claiming the shell failed to open (#2639); UI labels are translated to English (#2657)
  • node-agent: an opt-in vm-console source collects Fast Sandbox guest console output — node-local VM discovery from driver-written fast-sandbox.json without CR watches, raw-byte fidelity per sandbox UID across placement changes, and restart-safe acknowledged offsets (#2234); the integration environment deploys it and asserts collection end to end (#2676); ops guidance covers path alignment, node coverage, and discovery rules (#2677)
  • CLI: non-table configuration sections are rejected with a clear error instead of crashing every command (#2551); None table cells render as - instead of the literal text (#2691); an empty egress rule target is a usage error with the ACTION=TARGET hint (#2692)
  • OSEP-0025 follow-up: resolver caller authentication is specified — a cached Ed25519 JWT on every TCP resolve dial, verified offline against a server-published JWKS, closing the deferred R4 gap at the application layer (#2631)
  • Governance: maintainer nomination and removal rules are tightened — majority approval for component maintainers, path-owner support, sponsor LGTMs, and an emeritus/removal process (#2678); @jianpingpei is nominated as node-agent maintainer (#2679)
  • OSEPs and docs: OSEP-0024/0026 and six earlier OSEPs are marked implemented, OSEP-0006 (developer console) is withdrawn (#2624 #2670 #2671 #2672 #2673); the OSEP index page is removed from the docs site — oseps/ on GitHub is the canonical index (#2674)

Upgrade & Compatibility

  • Breaking: unknown fields in closed request objects now return 422 — previously ignored keys (for example readonly on a volume) are rejected; send each field once, alias or snake_case but not both; in the TypeScript SDK, ImageAuth.token combined with username/password now fails — send only username and password (#2576)
  • Deprecation: the server-proxied data path (/sandboxes/{id}/proxy/{port}, use_server_proxy, the SDK/CLI/MCP options) is in maintenance mode — no new features, security and bug fixes only; expose sandbox traffic through the ingress gateway (#2548)
  • Behavior change: code in a foreground isolated run can no longer read the session's stdin (it only ever got the run's own script that way), and a syntax error now ends the run with status 2 while the session survives — previously it killed the shell (#2517)
  • Behavior change: downloads of a directory return 400 INVALID_REQUEST_BODY instead of a filesystem-dependent 500 or an empty/incomplete 200/206; use the /directories/list route; a malformed-range 416 gains a message field (#2451)
  • Behavior change: idle-pause activity probe answers must be uncompressed, at most 4 KiB, and complete within timeoutSeconds as a whole-exchange bound — anything else is an error verdict for that candidate (#2596)
  • Behavior change: pools whose idle pod count exceeds a lowered poolMax now scale the excess in (only idle pods are deleted) (#2470)
  • Fast Sandbox: OCI-enabled deployments reserve an idle ublk device pool by default — set runtime.oci.poolLow=0 to keep the previous on-demand behavior, and match poolSizeGB to the built template capacity for custom disk sizes (#2594)
  • Fast Sandbox: port-scoped egress rules (NetworkRule.ports) are now accepted and enforced on fast-sandbox routes — they previously returned 400; existing rules are unaffected (#2662)
  • Experimental egress live revision runtime only: extra interception ports are rejected at startup — remove OPENSANDBOX_EGRESS_MITMPROXY_EXTRA_PORTS when enabling that runtime (#2587)
  • Experimental fast-sandbox revision runtime only (OPENSANDBOX_EGRESS_EXPERIMENTAL_REVISION_RUNTIME=true): the data-plane-ready hook may return 503 until the subject snapshot is acknowledged; creates then wait up to fastpath_wait_ready_seconds (default 30 s) and return Pending/Unavailable (#2666)
  • Images: opensandbox/<component>:release-1.2.1-rc.2 (all three registries; fsb images for fast-sandbox)
  • Packages: unchanged — SDK/CLI artifacts publish at the 1.2.1 stable release
